chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

regarding a crop that was sold while it was grass, then it became grain. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem when he says, 'I am buying from you what comes out from this crop'. So when he buys it and it is grass, if he wishes he can use it up (as grass), and if he wishes he can wait for it (to become grain).

key_terms.أَعْفَاهُ: he utilized it / cleared it (as grass)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling crops while they are still green or grassy?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the sale of unripe crops (bay' al-hasil) provided the commodity is clearly defined as 'what emerges' from the field, thereby avoiding the gharar (uncertainty) of selling the entire plant before its nature is determined. It highlights the buyer's discretion to either harvest the crop early as fodder or wait for full maturation, reflecting the practical agricultural jurisprudence of the time. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between valid conditional sales and prohibited speculative transactions in trade.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Al Musanna Al Hannat, from Zurara, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a farm which is sold and it is grass, then it sprouts. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when he says, ‘I am buying from you what comes out from this farm’. So when he buys it and it is grass, so if he so desires to he utilises it, and if he so desires to he waits (for harvest)’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Muthanna’ al- Hannat from Zurarah who has said the following: “About the case of a plantation which is sold when it is only grass, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not unlawful if he says, “I buy from you what comes out of this plantation.” If he buys it when it is only grass he can use it or if he likes he can wait (until harvest time).”’
